title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed

The divergences noted in the last newsletter have now materialized, and the market has shifted into pullback mode. After a strong 4–5 session surge, the large-cap indices have begun to retrace but are still holding above their rising 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages — keeping the primary trend intact for the large-cap leaders. Small caps remain stuck in a multi-week range but continue to hold above their 20- and 50-day moving averages for now. The mid-cap index, however, is materially weaker, sitting below all three key moving averages. This split action — strength in large caps and continued sloppiness in mids/smalls — reflects rotation and selectivity rather than a broad foundation of support.

Internals reinforce the caution. New lows are outpacing new highs by more than 2-to-1, and downside momentum is exceeding upside momentum by over 3-to-1. As participation narrows, long-side edge diminishes — breakouts become less reliable, follow-through weakens, and failed patterns increase. This is the type of environment where chasing strength late or forcing exposure tends to carry poor expectancy.

Sector behavior mirrors the tone. Technology, Healthcare, Materials, Utilities, and Industrials sit atop the relative-strength rankings. But leadership is thin — Technology is the only group decisively above both its 10- and 20-day moving averages. Seven of eleven sectors sit below their short-term trend levels, reflecting broad pressure. Only Technology and Energy currently maintain both relative strength and trend alignment. Focus should remain on sectors and setups that not only lead, but maintain structural integrity and constructive price behavior.

Taken together, the longer-term uptrend remains intact, but near-term conditions reflect weakening participation, rotational stress, and a tightening runway for upside traction. This is a time for patience, precision, and disciplined execution — leaning into strength early and avoiding the temptation to chase strength late as the tape adjusts.

Overall Trend: Mixed

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Negative

  • Small Cap: Negative

Overall NH/NL Breadth: Negative

  • Large Cap: Negative

  • Mid Cap: Negative

  • Small Cap: Negative

Overall Up/Down Momentum: Negative

  • Large Cap: Negative

  • Mid Cap: Negative

  • Small Cap: Negative

Market Recap

Market Monitor (Click Here)

1. Trend & Market Structure

The market remains in an overall uptrend on a higher-timeframe basis, but near-term conditions have weakened. Large-caps are still holding above key moving averages, while mid-caps are below all key MAs, and small-caps remain range-bound.

  • Maintain reduced and selective exposure given the mixed structure

  • Favor large-cap strength while mid- and small-caps lag

  • If two or more indices break below their 20-day MAs on volume, shift more defensive by raising cash and tightening stops

  • If indices reclaim and hold recent breakout levels with volume, gradually scale risk back up

2. Breadth & Momentum Watch

Internals have deteriorated meaningfully — fewer stocks are participating and downside momentum has picked up.

  • New lows > new highs (2-to-1+)

  • Downside momentum > upside momentum (3-to-1+)

  • Breakouts carry higher failure risk in this backdrop

Implications:

  • Treat conditions as lower-expectancy for long setups

  • Be quick to take profits and cut lagging trades

  • Monitor for improvement: a clear NH/NL expansion and upside momentum thrust would justify scaling exposure back up

3. Sector Allocation & Focus

Sector leadership remains narrow and selective.

Favor Leadership Where Trend & RS Align

  • Technology

Focus on names holding above key MAs and respecting structure.

Monitor for Turnaround (only with confirmation)

  • Healthcare

  • Materials

  • Utilities

  • Industrials

  • Consumer Cyclicals

  • Energy

  • Financials

Avoid sectors and stocks that are below key moving averages with a sloppy structure.

4. Stock Selection & Execution

With breadth weak and volatility picking up, precision matters more than participation.

✅ Focus on:

  • Tight bases near rising moving averages

  • High-liquidity leaders holding 10-/20-/50-day support

  • Pullbacks into logical support vs. chasing breakouts

❌ Avoid:

  • Extended names

  • Breakouts without strong volume confirmation

  • Thin/speculative stocks — low odds in this tape

Execution Rules

  • Take partial profits ⅓–½ at 2–3R or after 3–5 days

  • Move stop to breakeven after partial

  • Trail remainder using close below 10- or 20-day MA

  • Exit faster if trades stall — do not “hope and hold” in a weakening tape

5. Risk & Position Management

  • Keep 40–60% exposure until breadth improves

  • Hold 25–35% cash as optionality

  • Position sizing ½ to ¾ normal

  • Stops just below swing lows or 20-day MA

Your edge is capital preservation + readiness to scale when conditions reset.

6. Scenario Planning

  1. Breadth and momentum improve, indices reclaim highs: Scale exposure gradually, rotate into improving groups

  2. Status quo: mixed breadth, rotational chop: Stay selective, modest exposure, trade only best setups

  3. Internals weaken further, indices break MAs: Reduce exposure, raise cash to 40–50%, tighten stops

Bottom Line

The market remains in an uptrend, but internal weakness, rotation stress, and mid-cap breakdowns suggest a selective approach and heightened caution. Trade only your best setups, keep risk tight, and be prepared to adapt quickly as internals confirm or reject this pullback.
